title: Spinach & Cheddar Omelette
steps: Shred the cheddar if it is not already grated, roughly chop the 1 cup of spinach, and set both next to the stove so everything is ready once the eggs hit the pan.
Crack the 3 eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt, and whisk with a fork for about 30 seconds until the yolks and whites are fully blended with no streaks.
Melt 1/2 tablespoon of the butter in a 8-inch nonstick pan over medium heat. Add the spinach and cook, stirring, for 1 minute until just wilted, then tip it onto a plate.

Return the pan to medium-low heat and melt the remaining butter until it foams. Pour in the eggs and let them sit for 15 seconds, then drag the edges toward the center with a spatula, tilting the pan so the raw egg runs underneath.
When the top is mostly set but still a little glossy, about 2 minutes, scatter the spinach and cheddar over one half of the omelette.
Fold the empty half over the filling, cook 30 seconds more so the cheese melts, then slide onto a plate and serve right away.

title: Classic Scrambled Eggs on Toast
steps: Crack the 4 eggs into a bowl, add a pinch each of salt and pepper, and whisk well for about 30 seconds until completely smooth and slightly frothy.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over low heat until it just begins to foam, without letting it brown.
Pour in the eggs and let them sit for about 20 seconds until the edges barely start to set. Then stir slowly with a spatula, pushing the curds from the edges to the center.

Keep stirring gently for 3 to 4 minutes, lifting the pan off the heat for a few seconds if it gets too hot. Stop when the eggs look soft, creamy, and just set but still a little wet, since they will keep cooking.
Toast the 2 slices of bread while the eggs cook, until golden brown and crisp at the edges.
Pile the eggs onto the hot toast, finish with another pinch of pepper, and eat immediately.

title: Egg Fried Rice
steps: Slice the 2 green onion stalks thinly, keeping the white and green parts separate. Break up any clumps in the 2 cups of cooked rice with your fingers, since cold, dry rice fries best.
Beat the 2 eggs with a pinch of salt in a small bowl until the yolks are fully broken up.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the white parts of the green onion and stir for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Push the onion to one side, pour in the eggs, and stir gently for 30 to 45 seconds until they are softly scrambled and just set. Break them into small pieces.
Add the rice and spread it across the pan. Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, tossing occasionally, until the grains are hot and a few start to turn lightly golden.
Drizzle the soy sauce around the edges of the pan and toss for 30 seconds until the rice is evenly coloured. Stir in the green parts of the onion and serve hot.

title: Veggie Fried Rice
steps: Mince the 2 garlic cloves and break up any clumps in the 2 cups of cooked rice. Beat the 2 eggs with a pinch of salt in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the garlic and stir for 20 to 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Add the 1 cup of frozen vegetables straight from the freezer and cook, stirring often, for 3 to 4 minutes until thawed, hot, and any extra moisture has cooked off.
Push the vegetables to one side and pour the eggs into the cleared space. Stir for about 30 seconds until just set, then mix them into the vegetables.
Add the rice and spread it out. Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, tossing occasionally, until steaming and starting to crisp in spots.
Pour the soy sauce around the edge of the pan, toss everything for 30 seconds until evenly coated, and taste for salt and pepper before serving.

title: Garlic Butter Pasta
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil and stir in 1 teaspoon of salt. Meanwhile, mince the 4 garlic cloves finely and grate the parmesan if needed.
Add the 8 oz of pasta and cook, stirring occasionally, for 1 to 2 minutes less than the package time, until just al dente with a slight bite at the center.
Before draining, scoop out about 1/2 cup of the starchy pasta water, then drain the pasta.
In the same pot, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and cook for 45 to 60 seconds, stirring constantly, until fragrant and pale gold. Do not let it brown or it will turn bitter.
Add the pasta back with a splash of the pasta water and toss for 1 minute so the butter and water cling to the noodles in a glossy sauce.
Take the pot off the heat, add the parmesan, and toss until melted and smooth, adding more pasta water a tablespoon at a time if it looks dry. Finish with pepper and serve hot.

title: Tomato Basil Spaghetti
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 teaspoon of salt. Thinly slice the 3 garlic cloves and tear the basil leaves by hand, saving a few for garnish.
Warm the olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and cook for about 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant and barely golden.

Pour in the can of tomatoes, crushing them with the back of a spoon, and add a pinch of pepper. Simmer over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens and darkens slightly.
While the sauce simmers, cook the 8 oz of spaghetti in the boiling water until al dente, usually 8 to 10 minutes. Reserve 1/2 cup of the pasta water before draining.
Add the drained spaghetti to the skillet and toss over medium heat for 1 minute, adding a splash of pasta water if the sauce is too thick, until every strand is coated.
Stir in most of the basil, taste for salt, and serve topped with the reserved leaves.

title: Pesto Pasta
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Halve the 1 cup of cherry tomatoes and grate the parmesan if needed.
Cook the 8 oz of pasta until al dente, following the package time, usually 9 to 11 minutes. Scoop out about 1/2 cup of the pasta water before draining.
Return the drained pasta to the warm pot off the heat. Add the pesto and a few tablespoons of pasta water and toss until the noodles are evenly coated and the sauce looks creamy rather than oily.
Fold in the cherry tomatoes and toss for 30 seconds so they warm through without breaking down.
Stir in half the parmesan and loosen with more pasta water if needed. Taste for salt and pepper, then serve topped with the remaining parmesan.

title: Creamy Mushroom Pasta
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Wipe the mushrooms clean and slice them about 1/4 inch thick, mince the 3 garlic cloves, and grate the parmesan.
Cook the 8 oz of pasta until al dente, usually 9 to 11 minutes. Reserve 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain.

While the pasta cooks, melt the butter with a splash of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and cook, stirring only occasionally, for 6 to 8 minutes until the liquid has evaporated and they are deeply golden. Season with salt and pepper.
Lower the heat to medium, add the garlic, and stir for 30 to 45 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the 3/4 cup of heavy cream and simmer gently for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Add the pasta and parmesan to the skillet and toss for 1 minute, loosening with pasta water as needed, until the sauce is silky and clings to every piece. Serve immediately.

title: Stovetop Mac and Cheese
steps: Shred the 1 1/2 cups of cheddar yourself if you can, since freshly shredded melts more smoothly than pre-shredded. Bring a pot of water to a boil with 1 teaspoon of salt.
Cook the 8 oz of macaroni for 1 minute less than the package directs, usually 6 to 7 minutes, until tender but still firm. Drain, but do not rinse.
Return the empty pot to low heat and melt the butter. Pour in the 3/4 cup of milk and warm it for 1 to 2 minutes until steaming but not boiling.
Add the macaroni back to the pot and stir for 1 minute so it absorbs some of the milk and the sauce begins to thicken slightly.
Take the pot off the heat, add the cheddar a handful at a time, and stir until each addition has melted before adding the next, giving a smooth, glossy sauce.
Season with pepper and more salt to taste. Let it rest for 2 minutes to thicken, then serve hot.

title: Chicken & Broccoli Stir-Fry
steps: Slice the 1 lb of chicken breast across the grain into thin strips about 1/4 inch thick, and pat dry with paper towels. Cut the broccoli into bite-size florets and mince the 3 garlic cloves.
Toss the chicken with a pinch each of salt and pepper and 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, and let it sit while the pan heats.

Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat until it just begins to smoke. Add the chicken in a single layer and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through with no pink in the center. Transfer to a plate.
Add the broccoli and 2 tablespoons of water to the same pan, cover, and steam for 2 to 3 minutes until bright green and just tender-crisp.
Uncover, add the garlic, and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Return the chicken to the pan and pour in the remaining 2 tablespoons of soy sauce.
Toss everything for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce coats the chicken and slightly reduces. Serve over the 2 cups of warm cooked rice.

title: Lemon Garlic Chicken
steps: Pat the chicken breasts dry and, if they are thick, slice each in half horizontally so they cook evenly at about 1/2 inch thick. Mince the 4 garlic cloves and juice the lemon.
Season both sides generously with the salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the butter with a drizzle of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until foaming. Add the chicken and cook undisturbed for 5 to 6 minutes until deeply golden on the bottom.
Flip, reduce the heat to medium, and cook another 4 to 5 minutes until the chicken is cooked through with no pink inside and the juices run clear. Move it to a plate and cover loosely.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, add the remaining butter and the garlic, and stir for 30 to 45 seconds until fragrant. Pour in the lemon juice and scrape up the browned bits from the pan.
Simmer for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce is slightly thickened, return the chicken to the pan, and spoon the sauce over the top before serving.

title: Chicken Quesadillas
steps: Pull or chop the 2 cups of rotisserie chicken into small bite-size pieces, discarding any skin or bones, and make sure the cheddar is shredded.
Lay the 4 tortillas on a clean surface. Sprinkle one half of each with about 1/4 cup cheddar, then top with chicken and a spoonful of salsa.
Cover with a final sprinkle of cheese, which helps glue the filling together, and fold each tortilla in half.
Heat a large dry skillet over medium heat. Cook 1 or 2 quesadillas at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, pressing gently with a spatula, until the underside is golden brown and crisp.
Flip carefully and cook another 2 minutes until the second side is golden and the cheese is fully melted.
Rest on a cutting board for 1 minute, slice into wedges, and serve with extra salsa.

title: Cheese Quesadilla
steps: Shred the 1 cup of cheddar if needed. Lay the 2 tortillas flat on a clean surface.
Sprinkle the cheese evenly over one half of each tortilla, leaving a small border at the edge, and spoon the salsa over the cheese if you want it inside.
Fold each tortilla in half and press down gently.
Heat a large dry skillet over medium heat. Place the quesadillas in the pan and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the bottom is golden brown with a few darker spots.
Flip and cook for another 2 minutes until the cheese has melted completely and the second side is crisp. Slice into wedges and serve with the rest of the salsa for dipping.

title: Black Bean Tacos
steps: Drain and rinse the can of black beans in a colander until the water runs clear. Halve and pit the avocado, scoop it into a bowl, and cut the lime into wedges.
Warm a small saucepan over medium heat and add a drizzle of oil. Add the beans, 1 teaspoon of cumin, a pinch of salt, and 2 tablespoons of water.
Simmer for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring and mashing about a quarter of the beans with a spoon, until the mixture is thick and fragrant.
Mash the avocado with a fork, squeeze in the juice of half the lime, and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Heat a dry skillet over medium-high heat and warm each of the 6 tortillas for 20 to 30 seconds per side until soft and lightly charred in spots.
Fill each tortilla with beans, a spoonful of avocado, and salsa, then serve with the remaining lime wedges for squeezing over.

title: Beef Tacos
steps: Shred the lettuce into thin ribbons and make sure the cheddar is shredded. Set both aside in separate bowls.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 1 lb of ground beef and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon, until fully browned with no pink remaining. Spoon off any excess fat.

Sprinkle in the 2 tablespoons of taco seasoning and add 1/4 cup of water. Simmer over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until the liquid has mostly reduced and the beef is coated in a thick sauce.
Warm each of the 8 tortillas in a dry skillet over medium-high heat for about 20 seconds per side until pliable and lightly toasted.
Fill each tortilla with a generous spoonful of beef, then top with the cheddar and shredded lettuce. Serve right away while the beef is hot.

title: Tuna Melt
steps: Drain the can of tuna very well, pressing out the liquid, and flake it into a bowl. Stir in the 2 tablespoons of mayonnaise and a pinch each of salt and pepper until combined.
Divide the tuna mixture between 2 slices of bread, spreading it to the edges, and top each with a slice of cheddar. Close the sandwiches with the other 2 slices.

Heat a large skillet over medium-low heat and add a little oil. Cook the sandwiches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, pressing lightly, until the bread is deeply golden and the cheese has melted. Slice in half and serve hot.

title: Grilled Cheese & Tomato
steps: Slice the tomato into 1/4-inch rounds and pat them dry with paper towels so the sandwich does not get soggy. Spread the butter on one side of each of the 4 bread slices.

Place 2 slices butter side down in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Top each with a slice of cheddar, a layer of tomato, a pinch of salt and pepper, and another slice of cheddar, then close with the remaining bread, butter side up.

Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the bottom is golden brown, then flip and cook another 3 minutes, pressing gently, until the cheese is fully melted and the second side is crisp. Rest for 1 minute, then slice and serve.

title: Avocado Toast with Egg
steps: Halve and pit the avocado, scoop the flesh into a bowl, and mash it with a fork leaving some small chunks. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon half and season with salt and pepper.
Toast the 2 bread slices until golden brown and firm enough to hold the toppings.

Heat a nonstick skillet with a little oil over medium heat. Crack in the 2 eggs and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the whites are set and opaque but the yolks are still runny. For a firmer yolk, flip and cook 30 seconds more.
Spread the avocado generously over each slice of toast, then slide an egg on top. Finish with a pinch of salt and pepper and eat immediately.

title: Caprese Salad
steps: Take the mozzarella out of its liquid, pat it dry with paper towels, and let it come close to room temperature for about 10 minutes for better flavor.
Slice the 2 tomatoes and the 8 oz of mozzarella into 1/4-inch rounds, discarding the end pieces of tomato if they are tough.
Arrange the tomato and mozzarella on a platter, alternating and slightly overlapping them, and tuck whole basil leaves between the slices.
Drizzle with the olive oil, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and some pepper, and serve right away while the tomatoes are cool and the cheese is soft.

title: Greek Salad
steps: Cut the cucumber into 1/2-inch chunks, quarter or slice the 2 tomatoes into bite-size wedges, and slice the 1/4 red onion as thinly as you can. Soak the onion in cold water for 5 minutes to soften its bite, then drain well.
Place the cucumber, tomatoes, and drained onion in a large bowl.
Add the olive oil, oregano, a pinch of salt, and a little pepper, and toss gently for 30 seconds until everything is lightly coated.
Crumble the 1/2 cup of feta over the top in large pieces and serve right away, or chill for 10 minutes to let the flavors blend.

title: Chickpea Curry
steps: Finely dice the onion and mince the 3 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse the can of chickpeas in a colander.
Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent with golden edges.
Stir in the garlic and the 2 tablespoons of curry powder and cook for 1 minute until very fragrant, adding a splash of water if it starts to stick.
Add the chickpeas and the can of coconut milk, scraping up anything stuck to the bottom. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, uncovered, for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and creamy and clings to the chickpeas. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve spooned over the 2 cups of warm cooked rice.

title: Lentil Soup
steps: Rinse the 1 cup of lentils in a fine strainer and pick out any debris. Dice the onion, carrots, and celery into small 1/4-inch pieces so they cook evenly.
Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery with a pinch of salt and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until softened and the onion is translucent.
Stir in the 1 teaspoon of cumin and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the lentils, the 4 cups of broth, and 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a steady simmer.
Cover partially and cook for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are completely tender and the soup has thickened. Add more water if it becomes too thick.
Taste and adjust with salt and pepper. For a creamier texture, mash some of the soup against the side of the pot with a spoon before serving.

title: Tomato Soup
steps: Roughly chop the onion and mince the 2 garlic cloves.
Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent but not browned.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 to 45 seconds until fragrant. Pour in the can of tomatoes, including the juices, and the 2 cups of broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, partially covered, for 20 minutes until the onion is completely tender and the flavors have blended.
Blend the soup until completely smooth, using an immersion blender or by working in batches in a regular blender with the lid vented to let steam escape.
Return to low heat, stir in the 1/2 cup of cream, and warm for 2 minutes without boiling. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Roasted Potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and place a rimmed baking sheet inside while it heats. Scrub the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch chunks so they cook at the same rate.
Pat the potatoes dry with a clean towel, then toss in a large bowl with the olive oil, the salt, and a few grinds of pepper until every piece is glossy.
Carefully pull out the hot baking sheet and spread the potatoes in a single layer, cut sides down, without crowding. Roast for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, smash the garlic cloves lightly with the flat of a knife and strip the rosemary leaves from the sprigs.
Flip the potatoes, scatter the garlic and rosemary over the top, and roast for 15 to 20 minutes more until the outsides are deep golden and crisp and a fork slides easily into the centers.
Taste for salt and serve hot straight from the pan.

title: Sheet Pan Sausage & Veggies
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Cut the sausage into 1-inch pieces, slice the 2 bell peppers and the onion into 1-inch strips, and cut the potatoes into 3/4-inch cubes, since potatoes take the longest.
On a large rimmed baking sheet, toss the potatoes with half the olive oil, half the paprika, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread them out and roast for 10 minutes.
In a bowl, toss the peppers and onion with the remaining olive oil and paprika and a pinch of salt.
Remove the pan, add the vegetables and sausage, and stir to combine, spreading everything in a single layer with some space between the pieces so it roasts rather than steams.
Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the potatoes are tender and golden, the vegetables have charred edges, and the sausage is browned and cooked through.
Let it rest for 2 minutes, then serve directly from the pan.

title: Honey Garlic Salmon
steps: Take the salmon out of the fridge 10 minutes ahead, pat the fillets dry, and season both sides with salt and pepper. Mince the 3 garlic cloves and juice the 1/2 lemon.
Whisk the 2 tablespoons of honey, 2 tablespoons of soy sauce, garlic, and lemon juice together in a small bowl until smooth.

Heat a drizzle of oil in a large nonstick or oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Place the fillets in the pan skin side up and sear undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes until deeply golden.

Flip the fillets, reduce the heat to medium-low, and pour in the sauce. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, spooning the sauce over the fish, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and the sauce is thick and syrupy.
Transfer to plates, spoon the pan sauce over the top, and serve immediately.

title: Garlic Shrimp
steps: Peel the shrimp if needed, devein them, and pat completely dry with paper towels so they sear instead of steam. Season with salt and pepper. Mince the 4 garlic cloves, chop the parsley, and juice the 1/2 lemon.
Heat a drizzle of oil with 1 tablespoon of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until foaming.
Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook for 1 to 2 minutes without moving until pink and lightly golden on the bottom. Flip and cook 1 minute more, then transfer to a plate.

Lower the heat to medium, add the remaining butter and the garlic, and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Return the shrimp, add the lemon juice, and toss for 30 seconds until coated. Sprinkle with parsley and serve right away.

title: Tofu Teriyaki Bowl
steps: Drain the tofu, wrap it in a clean towel, and press under a heavy pan for 15 minutes to remove excess water. Cut it into 3/4-inch cubes and cut the broccoli into small florets.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the tofu in a single layer and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until golden and crisp on most sides.
Move the tofu to one side, add the broccoli and 3 tablespoons of water, cover, and steam for 3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp.
Uncover and pour in the 1/4 cup of teriyaki sauce. Toss for 1 to 2 minutes over medium heat until the sauce bubbles, thickens, and glazes the tofu and broccoli.
Divide the 2 cups of warm cooked rice between bowls, top with the tofu and broccoli, and spoon any extra sauce from the pan over the top.

title: Banana Pancakes
steps: Peel the ripe banana and mash it in a large bowl with a fork until mostly smooth with a few small lumps. Whisk in the egg and the 1/3 cup of milk until well combined.
Add the 1/2 cup of flour and a pinch of salt and stir just until no dry streaks remain. A few small lumps are fine, and overmixing makes tough pancakes. Let the batter rest for 5 minutes.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes, then melt a little of the butter in the pan, swirling to coat.
Pour in about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until bubbles form on the surface and the edges look set and dry.
Flip and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more until golden brown and cooked through. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding butter as needed, and serve warm.

title: Yogurt Parfait
steps: Rinse the 1/2 cup of blueberries and pat them dry. Choose a tall glass or jar so you can see the layers.
Spoon about 1/3 cup of the yogurt into the bottom of the glass, then add a layer of granola and a scattering of blueberries.
Repeat the layers with the remaining yogurt, granola, and blueberries, finishing with a generous layer of berries on top.
Drizzle the 1 tablespoon of honey over the top and serve right away so the granola stays crunchy.

title: Peanut Butter Banana Toast
steps: Peel the banana and slice it into rounds about 1/4 inch thick.
Toast the 2 slices of bread until deep golden brown and crisp, about 2 to 3 minutes, so they can hold up to the toppings.

While the toast is still warm, spread 1 tablespoon of peanut butter on each slice all the way to the edges so it softens slightly. Arrange the banana rounds on top in an overlapping layer, drizzle with the honey, and eat right away.

title: Huevos Rancheros
steps: Drain and rinse the black beans, then chop the cilantro. Warm the beans in a small pot over medium-low heat for 4 minutes, mashing about half with a spoon until thick and creamy.
Pour the salsa into a small saucepan and simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes until slightly thickened and darker in color. Keep it on the lowest heat while you cook the rest.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Fry the tortillas one at a time for 30 to 45 seconds per side until lightly crisp at the edges but still bendable, and set them on a plate.

Add the remaining oil to the skillet and lower the heat to medium. Crack in the eggs and season with salt, then cook 3 minutes for set whites and runny yolks, or cover for 1 minute more for firmer yolks.
Spread a spoonful of beans on each tortilla and top with 2 eggs. Spoon the warm salsa over the whites and finish with cilantro.

title: Chicken Tinga Tacos
steps: Slice the onion thinly and mince the garlic. Pat the chicken thighs dry and cut them in half so they cook evenly.

Simmer the chicken in a pot of lightly salted water over medium heat for 15 to 18 minutes until cooked through and no pink remains. Lift it out, shred with two forks, and keep a splash of the cooking water.
Cook the onion in a dry large skillet over medium heat for 6 minutes, adding a splash of water if it sticks, until soft and golden. Stir in the garlic and chili powder for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Pour in the tomato sauce and 1/4 cup of the reserved cooking water and simmer for 5 minutes until it thickens and darkens. Add the shredded chicken and cook 5 minutes more until the sauce clings to the meat.

Warm the tortillas directly over a gas flame or in a dry skillet over medium-high heat for 20 seconds per side until pliable with a few brown spots. Fill with chicken and top with a spoonful of sour cream.

title: Chilaquiles Rojos
steps: Cut the tortillas into 6 wedges each and dice the onion. Shred the monterey jack if it is a block.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Fry the tortilla wedges in two batches for 2 to 3 minutes each until golden and stiff, then drain on paper towels.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp oil and reduce heat to medium. Cook the onion for 2 minutes until just soft, then add the salsa and simmer 3 minutes until bubbling and slightly thick.
Fold the chips into the salsa and toss for 1 minute so they soften at the edges but keep some crunch. Sprinkle with the cheese, cover, and let it melt for 1 to 2 minutes.
Fry the eggs in a separate nonstick pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until the whites are set and yolks still soft. Slide them on top of the chilaquiles and drizzle with sour cream.

title: Beef Burrito Bowl
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it with 2 cups water in a covered pot over low heat for 15 minutes after it comes to a boil. Rest it off the heat, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
While the rice cooks, drain and rinse the black beans. Halve the avocado, remove the pit, and slice the flesh; cut the lime into wedges.
Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it into crumbles, until no pink remains.
Stir in the taco seasoning and 1/4 cup water and simmer 2 minutes until the sauce coats the meat. Add the beans and heat through for 2 minutes.
Divide the rice between two bowls and top with the beef and beans, salsa, and avocado. Squeeze lime juice over everything.

title: Elote-Style Street Corn
steps: Husk the corn and remove the silk. Grate the parmesan and cut the lime in half.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the corn and cook 8 to 10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes, until charred in spots and bright yellow.
Stir the mayonnaise with the juice of half the lime and a pinch of salt in a small bowl until smooth.
Brush the hot corn all over with the mayonnaise mixture while it is still warm so it sticks.
Roll the corn in the grated parmesan, dust with chili powder, and serve with the remaining lime half squeezed over the top.

title: Shrimp Fajitas
steps: Peel and devein the shrimp if needed and pat them very dry. Slice the bell peppers and onion into thin strips, and halve the lime.
Toss the shrimp with the chili powder, cumin, and the juice of half the lime in a bowl. Let them sit for 5 minutes while the pan heats.

Heat a large skillet over high heat until it just begins to smoke, then add 1 tbsp oil. Cook the peppers and onion for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring only occasionally, until charred at the edges and tender-crisp. Move them to a plate.
Add another splash of oil and the shrimp in a single layer. Cook 1 to 2 minutes per side until pink, curled, and opaque, then return the vegetables to the pan.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet for 20 seconds per side. Fill with shrimp and vegetables and squeeze the remaining lime over the top.

title: Orange Pork Carnitas Tacos
steps: Cut the pork into 1-inch chunks, discarding the bone and large fat pieces. Season the pork with the salt, cumin, and oregano and dice the onion finely.
Juice the orange. Place the pork, orange juice, and 1/2 cup water in a medium skillet over medium heat and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pork is fork-tender. Uncover and cook 8 to 10 minutes more until the liquid has evaporated.
Add 1 tbsp oil and turn the heat to medium-high. Sear the pork for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until the edges are browned and crispy, then break up large pieces with a spoon.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet for 20 seconds per side. Pile the carnitas into the tortillas and top with the diced onion.

title: Cheese Enchiladas with Red Sauce
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and lightly grease a small baking dish. Shred the cheese, dice the onion, and mince the garlic.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 3 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and chili powder and stir 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the tomato sauce plus 1/4 cup water and simmer for 8 minutes until slightly thickened. Season with a pinch of salt.
Warm each tortilla in a dry skillet for 15 seconds per side, then dip it in the sauce so it is lightly coated. Fill with a handful of cheese and roll it up, placing it seam-side down in the dish.
Pour the remaining sauce over the enchiladas and sprinkle with the rest of the cheese. Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling at the edges.

title: Margherita Pizza
steps: Set a baking sheet or pizza stone in the oven and heat to 500°F for at least 15 minutes. Let the dough sit at room temperature for 20 minutes so it stretches easily.
Tear the mozzarella into small pieces and pat dry with paper towels so the pizza does not turn soggy. Stir a pinch of salt into the tomato sauce.
Stretch the dough on a floured sheet of parchment into a 10 to 12 inch round, working from the center outward with your fingertips.
Spread the sauce thinly, leaving a 1/2 inch border, and scatter the mozzarella over it. Drizzle with half the olive oil.
Slide the parchment onto the hot sheet and bake 8 to 10 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling with brown spots. Top with torn basil and the remaining olive oil.

title: Chicken Parmesan
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally into two thin cutlets and pound them to 1/2 inch thick between sheets of plastic wrap.
Beat the egg in a shallow dish and mix the breadcrumbs with the parmesan and a pinch of salt in another. Dip each cutlet in egg, then press firmly into the breadcrumbs.
Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the cutlets for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden brown.
Spoon the marinara over the cutlets and top each with mozzarella. Transfer the skillet to the oven.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes until the cheese is melted and the chicken reaches 165°F inside. Let it rest 3 minutes before serving.

title: Lemon Parmesan Risotto
steps: Warm the chicken broth in a small saucepan over low heat and keep it hot. Dice the onion finely, grate the parmesan, and zest and juice the lemon.
Heat the olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the edges look glassy. Pour in a ladle of broth and stir until it is mostly absorbed.

Keep adding broth one ladle at a time, stirring often, for 20 to 25 minutes total, waiting until each addition is mostly absorbed. The rice is done when it is creamy but still slightly firm in the center.
Remove from the heat and stir in the remaining butter, parmesan, lemon zest, and 1 tbsp lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper and rest 2 minutes before serving.

title: Tomato Bruschetta
steps: Dice the tomatoes into small cubes and drain off excess juice in a sieve for 5 minutes. Cut the garlic clove in half and tear or thinly slice the basil.
Toss the tomatoes with 1 tbsp olive oil, the balsamic vinegar, the basil, and a pinch of salt. Let the mixture rest while you toast the bread.
Brush the bread slices on both sides with the remaining olive oil. Toast in a skillet over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Rub the cut side of the garlic clove across the warm toast so it melts a little into the surface.
Spoon the tomato mixture onto the toast just before serving so the bread stays crunchy.

title: Eggplant Parmesan
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Slice the eggplant into 1/2 inch rounds, salt both sides lightly, and let them sit on paper towels for 10 minutes, then blot dry.
Beat the egg in a shallow dish and mix the breadcrumbs with half the parmesan on a plate. Dip each slice in egg, then coat in crumbs.
Arrange the slices on the sheet, drizzle with olive oil, and bake for 20 minutes, flipping once halfway, until golden and tender.
Lower the oven to 375°F. Spread a thin layer of marinara in a small baking dish, then layer the eggplant, more sauce, and mozzarella, repeating once.
Top with the remaining parmesan and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the cheese melts and the sauce bubbles around the edges. Let it stand 5 minutes before serving.

title: Hearty Minestrone
steps: Dice the onion, carrot, and celery into small even pieces. Drain and rinse the kidney beans.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot, and celery for 7 minutes, stirring, until the onion is soft and translucent.
Add the diced tomato and its juices, the broth, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the kidney beans and the pasta. Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the pasta is just tender.
Taste and adjust the salt. Ladle into bowls while hot.

title: Italian Sausage and Peppers
steps: Slice the bell peppers and onion into thick strips and thinly slice the garlic. Prick the sausages once or twice with a fork.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Brown the sausages for 8 minutes, turning, until deeply colored on all sides, then move them to a plate.
Add the peppers and onion to the same pan with a pinch of salt. Cook 8 minutes over medium heat, scraping up the browned bits, until soft and lightly caramelized.
Stir in the garlic and oregano for 30 seconds, then add the marinara and 2 tbsp water. Nestle the sausages back into the pan.
Cover and simmer on low for 10 minutes until the sausages reach 160°F inside and the sauce is thick.

title: Chicken Piccata
steps: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally and pound to 1/2 inch thick. Season both sides with the salt and some pepper, then dredge in the flour and shake off the excess.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the cutlets 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through, then move them to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and pour in the broth and the juice of 1 lemon, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until reduced by about half.
Whisk in the butter one tablespoon at a time until the sauce is glossy. Thinly slice the second lemon and add it to the pan.
Return the chicken to the pan and spoon the sauce over it for 1 minute to warm through.

title: Fluffy Blueberry Pancakes
steps: Melt 1 tbsp butter and let it cool slightly. Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar, and a pinch of salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl whisk the milk, egg, and melted butter. Pour into the dry ingredients and stir only until just combined; a few lumps are fine.
Fold in the blueberries gently. Let the batter rest for 5 minutes so it thickens.
Melt a little of the remaining butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake and cook 2 to 3 minutes until bubbles form on top and the edges look set.
Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more until golden and the center springs back when pressed. Repeat with the remaining batter and butter.

title: Cinnamon French Toast
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, cinnamon, and vanilla in a shallow dish until completely smooth with no streaks of egg white.
Soak each bread slice in the mixture for about 20 seconds per side so it absorbs the custard but is not falling apart.
Melt 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium heat until foaming.
Cook two slices at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden and the centers feel slightly firm.
Wipe the pan, add the remaining butter, and cook the rest of the slices. Serve hot with warm maple syrup.

title: Sausage Potato Breakfast Hash
steps: Cut the potatoes into 1/2 inch cubes, dice the onion and pepper, and remove the sausage from its casing.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes and salt and cook, stirring only every 2 to 3 minutes, for 10 to 12 minutes until golden and tender when pierced with a fork.
Push the potatoes to the side, add the sausage, and cook 4 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through.
Add the onion and pepper and cook 4 minutes more until softened, stirring everything together.
Make two wells in the hash, add a little oil, and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook 3 to 4 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft.

title: Sausage Gravy Biscuits
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Whisk 1 cup flour, the baking powder, and the salt in a bowl, then cut in 3 tbsp cold cubed butter with your fingers until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir in 1/2 cup milk just until a shaggy dough forms. Pat it out 1 inch thick on a floured surface and cut into 4 rounds.
Place the biscuits on a baking sheet and bake 12 to 14 minutes until tall and golden brown on top.
Meanwhile, brown the sausage in a skillet over medium heat for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains. Stir in the remaining butter and 3 tbsp flour and cook 1 minute.
Slowly pour in the remaining milk while whisking and simmer 4 to 5 minutes until thick and creamy. Season with black pepper and ladle over the split biscuits.

title: Classic Cheeseburger
steps: Divide the beef into two equal portions and gently shape each into a patty slightly wider than the bun. Press a shallow dimple in the center so they stay flat, then season both sides with salt and pepper.
Slice the onion into thin rings. Toast the buns cut-side down in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1 minute until golden, then set aside.
Heat a skillet or griddle over medium-high heat until very hot. Cook the patties for 3 to 4 minutes without moving them until a dark crust forms.
Flip, top each patty with a slice of cheese, and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until the cheese melts and the center reaches 160°F.
Spread ketchup and mustard on the buns, add the patties and onion rings, and close the burgers.

title: Crispy Bacon BLT
steps: Slice the tomato into thick rounds and pat them dry. Wash and dry the lettuce leaves.
Lay the bacon in a cold skillet and turn the heat to medium. Cook 8 to 10 minutes, turning occasionally, until evenly browned and crisp, then drain on paper towels.
Toast the bread slices in a toaster or a dry skillet for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Spread mayonnaise on one side of every slice of toast. Season the tomato slices with black pepper.
Layer lettuce, tomato, and bacon on two slices of toast, cover with the others, and cut each sandwich in half diagonally.

title: Glazed Meatloaf
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Dice the onion very finely.
Stir the breadcrumbs and milk together in a large bowl and let them soak for 3 minutes. Add the beef, egg, onion, worcestershire, salt, pepper, and 2 tbsp ketchup.
Mix gently with your hands only until combined, since overworking makes it tough. Shape into a loaf about 8 by 4 inches on the baking sheet.
Bake for 35 minutes, then spread the remaining ketchup over the top.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes more until the center reaches 160°F and the glaze is sticky and caramelized. Rest 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Loaded Baked Potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Scrub the potatoes, pierce them several times with a fork, rub with a little oil and half the salt, and place directly on the oven rack.
Bake 45 to 55 minutes until the skin is crisp and a knife slides into the center with no resistance.
While they bake, cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes until crisp, drain, and crumble. Thinly slice the green onions.
Split the hot potatoes open lengthwise, fluff the insides with a fork, and mash in the butter and remaining salt.
Top with the cheese and return to the oven for 3 minutes until melted. Finish with sour cream, bacon, and green onion.

title: Mapo Tofu
steps: Cut the tofu into 3/4-inch cubes and let them sit in a bowl of hot salted water for 5 minutes, then drain gently; this firms them so they do not break. Mince the garlic and ginger, slice the green onions, and stir the cornstarch into 1/4 cup cold water.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet or wok over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the ground beef and break it up, cooking 3 to 4 minutes until browned and crispy at the edges.
Push the beef aside, add the garlic, ginger and red pepper flake, and stir 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Pour in the soy sauce and 3/4 cup water, then slide in the tofu and simmer on medium-low for 5 minutes, shaking the pan rather than stirring so the cubes stay whole.
Stir the cornstarch slurry again and pour it in, simmering 1 minute until the sauce turns glossy and coats a spoon.
Scatter the green onions on top and serve over steamed rice while piping hot.

title: Beef and Broccoli
steps: Slice the steak thinly against the grain, then toss with 1 tsp of the soy sauce and 1 tsp cornstarch and let it rest 10 minutes. Mince the garlic and ginger and cut the broccoli into bite-size florets.
Whisk the remaining soy sauce, brown sugar, 1 tsp cornstarch and 1/4 cup water into a sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide skillet over high heat until just smoking. Sear the beef in a single layer for 1 to 2 minutes per side until browned, then move it to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the broccoli with 2 tbsp water, cover, and steam 2 to 3 minutes until bright green and just tender.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir 20 seconds until fragrant.
Return the beef, pour in the sauce, and toss 1 minute until it thickens and clings to everything. Serve over rice.

title: Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
steps: Cut the tomatoes into wedges and slice the green onions, keeping the white and green parts separate. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt until streaky.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Pour in the eggs and let them set for 10 seconds, then gently push them into large soft curds; pull them out while still slightly wet, about 1 minute.
Add the remaining oil and the green onion whites and stir for 15 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, sugar and remaining salt, and cook 3 to 4 minutes, pressing lightly, until they break down into a saucy, juicy mixture.
Return the eggs and fold gently for 30 seconds so they absorb the tomato juice.
Top with the green onion tops and serve over hot rice.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
steps: Cut the chicken into 3/4-inch pieces and toss with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce and 1 tsp cornstarch; marinate 10 minutes. Dice the bell pepper and mince the garlic.
Whisk the remaining soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, remaining cornstarch and 3 tbsp water into a sauce.
Toast the cashews in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in the skillet over high heat. Add the chicken in one layer and sear 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through.
Add the bell pepper and garlic and stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes until the pepper is crisp-tender.
Pour in the sauce and toss 1 minute until glossy, then fold in the cashews and serve over rice.

title: Peanut Sesame Noodles
steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Cut the cucumber into matchsticks, slice the green onions and grate the garlic.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar and garlic with 3 tbsp hot water until smooth and pourable.
Cook the noodles about 3 minutes until tender with a slight chew, then drain and rinse briefly under warm water to stop clumping.
Toss the hot noodles with the sauce for 30 seconds until every strand is coated; loosen with a splash of water if it looks tacky.
Top with the cucumber and green onions and serve warm or chilled.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
steps: Cut the pork into 1-inch cubes, season with salt and black pepper, and toss with 1/4 cup of the cornstarch until dusty and dry. Chop the bell pepper into chunks.
Mix the ketchup, rice vinegar, sugar, remaining cornstarch and 1/4 cup water into a sauce.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until a pinch of cornstarch sizzles. Fry the pork 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked through, then drain on paper towels.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp oil. Add the bell pepper and pineapple and stir-fry 2 minutes until the pepper is crisp-tender.
Pour in the sauce and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until thick and glossy.
Add the pork, toss for 20 seconds so it stays crisp, and serve at once over rice.

title: Oyakodon
steps: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and thinly slice the onion. Lightly beat the eggs, leaving a few streaks of white.
In a small skillet, combine the soy sauce, sugar and 3/4 cup water and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the onion and chicken and simmer 6 to 8 minutes, turning once, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink.
Pour about two thirds of the egg evenly over the top, cover, and cook 1 minute on medium-low until just barely set.
Pour in the remaining egg, cover, and turn off the heat for 30 seconds so it stays soft and custardy.
Slide the contents over two bowls of hot rice, spooning the sauce on top.

title: Gyudon
steps: Freeze the steak for 15 minutes to firm it up, then slice it as thinly as possible. Cut the onion into thin half-moons and grate the ginger.
Combine the soy sauce, sugar, ginger and 3/4 cup water in a skillet and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the beef slices one at a time to separate them and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until no pink remains, skimming any foam.
Spoon the beef, onion and a generous amount of sauce over bowls of hot rice.

title: Chicken Katsu
steps: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally, pound to 1/2 inch thick, and season with salt and black pepper. Set up three plates: flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then press firmly into the breadcrumbs to coat both sides.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat until a breadcrumb sizzles on contact, about 340F.
Fry the cutlets 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden brown and cooked through, reaching 165F inside.
Drain on a rack or paper towels for 2 minutes so the crust stays crisp.
Stir the worcestershire sauce and ketchup together for a tonkatsu-style sauce, slice the cutlets, and serve with rice.

title: Yakisoba
steps: Shred the cabbage, cut the carrot into thin matchsticks and slice the onion. Whisk the soy sauce and worcestershire sauce together.
Cook the noodles in boiling water 2 minutes until just loosened, then drain and toss with a little oil to prevent sticking.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat until shimmering. Stir-fry the onion and carrot 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and cook 2 to 3 minutes until wilted with a few charred edges.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss constantly for 2 minutes until the noodles take on color and the pan looks dry. Serve hot.

title: Pork Shogayaki
steps: Slice the pork into thin strips and the onion into thin half-moons. Grate the ginger.
Mix the ginger, soy sauce, sugar and 2 tbsp water in a bowl and toss with the pork; rest 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Cook the onion 2 minutes until softened.
Lift the pork out of the marinade and add it to the pan, cooking 3 to 4 minutes until browned and no longer pink.
Pour in the leftover marinade and bubble 1 minute until it reduces to a sticky glaze.
Serve over rice with any shredded cabbage you have.

title: Tamagoyaki Rice Bowl
steps: Beat the eggs with the soy sauce and sugar until the sugar dissolves and no streaks of white remain. Slice the green onion.
Heat a small nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and wipe it with an oiled paper towel.
Pour in a thin layer of egg, about a third of it, and let it set until the surface is just wet, about 1 minute.
Roll the egg from one edge into a log, push it to the far side, oil the pan again and pour in another layer under the roll.
Repeat once more until all the egg is used, then cook the finished roll 30 seconds on each side.
Slice the roll into rounds and serve on rice topped with green onion.

title: Bibimbap
steps: Cut the carrot into matchsticks. Mix 1 tbsp of the soy sauce with 1 tsp sesame oil and set aside.
Brown the beef in a skillet over medium-high heat for 4 minutes until crumbled and cooked through, add the remaining soy sauce, and cook 1 minute more; transfer to a plate.
In the same pan with a drizzle of oil, saute the carrot 2 minutes until just tender, then set it aside.
Add the spinach with a splash of water and cook 1 minute until wilted; squeeze dry and toss with the soy-sesame mixture.
Fry the eggs in a little oil over medium heat 2 to 3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny.
Divide the rice between bowls, arrange the beef and vegetables on top, add an egg, and finish with sriracha and the remaining sesame oil. Mix everything together before eating.

title: Beef Bulgogi
steps: Freeze the steak for 15 minutes, then slice it paper-thin against the grain. Grate the pear and mince the garlic; slice the green onions.
Mix the pear, soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic and sesame oil into a marinade, then toss with the beef and rest at least 15 minutes.
Heat a large skillet over high heat until very hot, with 1 tbsp oil.
Cook the beef in two batches so it sears instead of steaming, 2 to 3 minutes per batch, until browned and caramelized at the edges.
Return everything to the pan with the green onions and toss 30 seconds.
Serve over rice or wrapped in lettuce leaves.

title: Korean Fried Chicken
steps: Cut the thighs into 2-inch pieces, pat very dry, season with salt and pepper, and toss with the cornstarch until each piece is fully coated.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350F over medium-high heat, which is when a pinch of cornstarch bubbles vigorously.
Fry the chicken in two batches for 5 to 6 minutes until pale golden, then drain on a rack for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, simmer the soy sauce, honey, sriracha and minced garlic in a small pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until syrupy.
Raise the oil to 375F and fry the chicken again for 2 to 3 minutes until deep golden and shatteringly crisp.
Toss the hot chicken in the glaze and serve right away.

title: Japchae
steps: Soak or cook the rice noodles per the package until tender, about 5 minutes, then drain and cut into shorter lengths with kitchen scissors. Cut the carrot and onion into thin strips and mince the garlic.
Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat and saute the carrot and onion 3 minutes until crisp-tender; remove to a bowl.
Add the spinach to the pan and cook 1 minute until wilted, then add the garlic for 15 seconds.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss over medium heat for 2 minutes until the noodles turn glossy and absorb the liquid.
Return the vegetables, toss together, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Steamed Egg Gyeran-jjim
steps: Beat the eggs thoroughly with the salt, then whisk in the water until fully combined. Strain through a sieve for a silky texture.
Slice the green onions finely.
Pour the mixture into a small heatproof bowl or pot, filling it no more than two thirds.
Set it over low heat with a lid slightly ajar and stir gently with a spoon for the first 2 minutes until the egg begins to clump.
Cover completely and cook 6 to 8 minutes on low until the top is set and puffed with a jiggle in the middle.
Drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle on the green onions before serving hot in the pot.

title: Spicy Pork Stir-Fry
steps: Slice the pork thinly, the onion into half-moons and the garlic finely. Mix the sriracha, soy sauce, sugar and garlic into a paste.
Toss the pork with the paste and marinate for 10 minutes while you prep the green onions.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and cook 2 minutes until beginning to soften.
Add the pork and stir-fry 4 to 5 minutes until browned at the edges, cooked through, and the sauce has caramelized onto the meat.
Garnish with green onions and serve with rice.

title: Pad Thai
steps: Soak the rice noodles in hot tap water for 15 to 20 minutes until flexible but still firm, then drain. Peel the shrimp, mince the garlic, cut the green onions into 1-inch lengths and quarter the lime.
Stir the fish sauce, sugar and 1 tbsp water together until the sugar dissolves.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat. Cook the shrimp 1 to 2 minutes until pink and curled, then remove.
Add another tbsp oil and the garlic and stir 10 seconds. Crack in the eggs and scramble for 30 seconds until just set.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss 2 to 3 minutes until the noodles are tender and have absorbed the liquid.
Return the shrimp, add the green onions, toss 30 seconds and serve with lime wedges.

title: Thai Basil Chicken
steps: Chop the chicken into small pieces, about 1/4 inch, or pulse briefly in a food processor. Mince the garlic and mix the soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar in a cup.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or skillet over high heat until smoking lightly.
Add the garlic for 10 seconds, then the chicken, and stir-fry 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through and lightly browned.
Pour in the sauce and cook 1 minute until it clings to the meat.
Turn off the heat and fold in the basil until just wilted.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil over medium-high heat until the edges are crisp and lacy, about 2 minutes, and serve on rice with the chicken.

title: Thai Coconut Chicken Curry
steps: Slice the chicken into thin strips, the bell pepper and onion into strips, and mince the garlic. Squeeze the lime.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pot over medium heat and soften the onion for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the garlic and curry powder and stir 1 minute until fragrant and slightly darker.
Pour in the coconut milk and 1/2 cup water, bring to a gentle simmer, and stir in the fish sauce.
Add the chicken and bell pepper and simmer 10 to 12 minutes, uncovered, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is slightly thickened.
Finish with the lime juice and serve over rice.

title: Vietnamese Noodle Salad
steps: Cook the rice noodles in boiling water 3 to 5 minutes until tender, then rinse under cold water and drain well.
Cut the cucumber and carrot into thin matchsticks and tear the mint leaves.
Whisk the juice of the limes, fish sauce, sugar, minced garlic and 3 tbsp water until the sugar dissolves for the dressing.
Divide the noodles between bowls and pile the cucumber, carrot and mint on top.
Pour over the dressing just before serving, toss, and taste for a balance of sweet, sour and salty.

title: Tom Kha Shrimp Soup
steps: Peel and devein the shrimp, slice the mushrooms, and thinly slice the ginger. Juice the limes and roughly chop the cilantro.
Combine the chicken broth, coconut milk and ginger in a pot and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat; avoid a hard boil which can split the coconut milk.
Simmer 8 minutes so the ginger flavors the broth.
Add the mushrooms and cook 4 minutes until tender.
Add the shrimp and cook 2 to 3 minutes until pink and opaque.
Turn off the heat, stir in the fish sauce and lime juice, and top with cilantro.

title: Quick Beef Pho
steps: Freeze the steak for 15 minutes, then slice it paper-thin. Halve the onion and slice the ginger into coins.
Char the onion and ginger in a dry pot over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until blackened in spots.
Add the broth and 1 cup water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer for 15 minutes so the aromatics infuse. Stir in the fish sauce.
Meanwhile, soak or cook the rice noodles per the package until tender, then drain and divide between two bowls.
Strain the broth, return it to a rolling boil, and lay the raw steak slices over the noodles.
Ladle the boiling broth into the bowls so the beef cooks to pink in 1 minute, then top with cilantro and a squeeze of lime.

title: Aloo Gobi
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 3/4-inch cubes. Cut the cauliflower into small florets, then dice the onion and mince the garlic and ginger.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the cumin and let it sizzle for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden at the edges. Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, turmeric and 1 teaspoon salt and stir to coat. Cook for 5 minutes, then add the cauliflower and 1/4 cup water.
Cover and cook on medium-low for 15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the potato.
Uncover, raise the heat to medium and cook 3 to 4 minutes until the water is gone and the edges brown slightly. Season with pepper and serve hot.

title: Saag Tofu
steps: Press the tofu between paper towels for 10 minutes, then cut into 1-inch cubes. Chop the onion finely and mince the garlic and ginger.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil and onion to the pan over medium heat. Cook 5 minutes until soft, then add garlic, ginger and cumin and stir for 1 minute.
Add the spinach in handfuls with 2 tablespoons water, stirring until fully wilted, about 4 minutes.
Blend the spinach mixture with a blender or immersion blender until mostly smooth, then return it to the pan over low heat.
Stir in the cream, tofu and 1/2 teaspoon salt and simmer gently for 4 minutes until heated through and glossy.

title: Butter Chicken
steps: Cut the chicken into 1-inch pieces and toss with the yogurt, 1/2 teaspoon salt and half the garlic. Let it sit for at least 10 minutes while you chop the onion and mince the ginger.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in a single layer for 6 minutes, turning once, until browned in spots, then remove it.
Add the remaining butter and the onion to the pan over medium heat. Cook 6 minutes until soft and golden, then add the remaining garlic and the ginger for 1 minute.
Pour in the tomato sauce and 1/4 cup water, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer 8 minutes until it darkens and thickens slightly.
Return the chicken to the pan and simmer on low for 10 minutes until it is cooked through and tender with no pink inside.
Stir in the cream and cook 2 minutes without boiling. Taste for salt and serve over rice.

title: Dal Tadka
steps: Rinse the lentils in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Dice the onion and tomato and mince the garlic.
Combine the lentils, water, turmeric and 1 teaspoon salt in a medium pot. Bring to a boil over high heat, skimming any foam.
Reduce to a gentle simmer, partly cover and cook 20 to 25 minutes until the lentils are soft and collapsing. Mash lightly with a spoon.
Meanwhile melt 1 tablespoon butter in a small pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until golden. Add the tomato and cook 4 minutes until jammy, then stir this into the lentils.
In the same pan melt the remaining butter over medium-high heat. Add the cumin and garlic and fry 30 to 45 seconds until the garlic is golden but not burnt.
Pour the sizzling tadka over the dal, stir once and serve with rice or bread.

title: Egg Curry
steps: Boil the eggs in a pot of boiling water for 9 minutes, then cool in cold water and peel. Dice the onion and tomatoes and mince the garlic and ginger.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until deep golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and 1/2 teaspoon salt and cook 6 minutes, mashing, until they break down into a thick paste.
Pour in the coconut milk and 1/2 cup water and simmer 5 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon.
Halve the eggs, slide them into the sauce and warm gently for 3 minutes, spooning sauce over the top.

title: Coconut Shrimp Curry
steps: Peel and devein the shrimp and pat dry. Dice the onion and mince the garlic and ginger, then cut the lime into wedges.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes until soft and translucent.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and curry powder and cook 1 minute until the spices smell toasty.
Pour in the coconut milk and 1/2 teaspoon salt, bring to a gentle simmer and cook 8 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the shrimp and cook 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until pink, curled and opaque throughout.
Squeeze in the juice of 2 lime wedges, taste for salt and serve over rice.

title: Shakshuka
steps: Dice the onion and bell pepper and mince the garlic. Crush the canned tomatoes with your hands or a fork.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper 8 minutes until very soft.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and stir 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the tomatoes with 1/2 teaspoon salt and simmer 10 minutes until thick and jammy.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook on low for 5 to 7 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still wobble.
Season with pepper and serve straight from the pan with bread.

title: Classic Hummus
steps: Drain the chickpeas and rinse well. Juice the lemon and peel the garlic.
Place the chickpeas in a small pot with water to cover and simmer over medium heat for 8 minutes so they turn very soft.
Drain and add them to a food processor with the garlic, lemon juice, cumin and salt. Blend 1 minute until crumbly.
With the motor running, add the water a tablespoon at a time, then 2 tablespoons olive oil, blending 2 minutes until smooth and creamy.
Scrape down the sides and taste, adding more salt or lemon if needed.
Spoon into a bowl, make a swirl with the back of a spoon and drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

title: Chicken Shawarma Pitas
steps: Slice the chicken into thin strips. Mince the garlic and dice the cucumber.
Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon olive oil, cumin, paprika, 2 minced garlic cloves and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Marinate for 15 minutes.
Stir together the yogurt, remaining garlic, cucumber and a pinch of salt to make a quick sauce.
Heat the remaining oil in a large skillet over high heat until shimmering. Cook the chicken in a single layer for 6 to 8 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Warm the pitas in a dry pan or microwave for 30 seconds until soft and pliable.
Fill each pita with chicken and a generous spoonful of the sauce and serve right away.

title: Baba Ganoush
steps: Heat the oven to 450 F. Prick the eggplants all over with a fork and set them on a lined baking sheet.
Roast for 35 to 40 minutes, turning once, until the skins are blackened and the flesh is collapsed and very soft.
Let them cool for 10 minutes, then slice open and scoop the flesh into a colander. Press gently and drain for 5 minutes to remove bitter liquid.
Mince the garlic and chop the parsley. Juice the lemon.
Mash the eggplant with a fork in a bowl, then stir in the garlic, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, cumin, salt and 2 tablespoons olive oil.
Spoon into a dish, drizzle with the remaining oil and top with parsley.

title: Couscous Tabbouleh
steps: Place the couscous in a heatproof bowl with 1/2 cup boiling water and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Cover tightly and let it steam 5 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and let it cool for 5 minutes.
Finely chop the parsley and mint, discarding thick stems. Dice the tomatoes and cucumber into small cubes.
Juice the lemon and whisk it with the olive oil and the remaining salt.
Toss the couscous with the herbs and vegetables, then pour the dressing over.
Rest for 10 minutes so the flavors meld, then season with pepper and serve.

title: Lemon Garlic Shrimp with Couscous
steps: Peel and devein the shrimp and pat dry. Mince the garlic, chop the parsley and zest then juice the lemon.
Pour 3/4 cup boiling water over the couscous with a pinch of salt and 1 teaspoon olive oil. Cover for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat the remaining olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet over medium-high heat until foaming.
Cook the shrimp in one layer for 2 minutes per side until pink and curled, then add the garlic for the last 30 seconds.
Add the remaining butter, lemon zest and juice and swirl for 1 minute to make a quick pan sauce.
Stir the parsley into the couscous and spoon the shrimp and sauce over the top.

title: Ratatouille
steps: Cut the eggplant, zucchini, bell pepper and tomatoes into 3/4-inch cubes. Dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the eggplant for 6 minutes until golden, then remove it.
Add the remaining oil and onion and cook 5 minutes over medium heat. Add the pepper and zucchini and cook 6 minutes more.
Stir in the garlic and thyme for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and 1 teaspoon salt.
Return the eggplant, cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything is tender and the juices have thickened.
Uncover and cook 5 minutes to reduce the liquid. Finish with pepper and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: French Onion Soup
steps: Halve the onions and slice them thinly. Shred the Swiss cheese and toast the bread slices until dry and crisp.
Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onions and salt and cook 40 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until deep brown and jammy.
If the bottom browns too fast, add a splash of water and scrape. The onions should look like dark mahogany ribbons.
Add the beef broth, thyme and bay leaf and bring to a boil. Simmer 10 minutes, then remove the bay leaf.
Heat the broiler. Ladle the soup into two oven-safe bowls, float a toast slice on each and pile the cheese on top.
Broil 3 to 4 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and browned in spots, then let cool 2 minutes before eating.

title: Potato Gratin
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F and butter a small baking dish. Peel the potatoes and slice them 1/8 inch thick, keeping them dry.
Smash the garlic and warm it in the cream in a small saucepan over medium heat for 3 minutes. Remove the garlic and stir in the nutmeg, thyme, 3/4 teaspoon salt and pepper.
Layer half the potatoes in the dish, overlapping slightly, and sprinkle with half the cheese.
Add the remaining potatoes and pour the warm cream over them, pressing down gently so the potatoes are mostly submerged.
Top with the remaining cheese, cover with foil and bake 30 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake 15 to 20 minutes more until the top is golden and a knife slides in easily. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

title: French Herb Omelette
steps: Finely chop the parsley and strip the thyme leaves. Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk with the salt and pepper until fully blended with no streaks.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat for 1 minute and melt half the butter until it foams.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently with a spatula for 20 seconds, pulling the edges inward as curds form.
When the eggs are mostly set but still glossy on top, about 1 minute, scatter the herbs and cheese over one half.
Fold the omelette in half and slide it out of the pan onto a plate, seam side down.
Rub the remaining butter over the top for shine and serve right away.

title: Butternut Squash Soup
steps: Peel the squash, scoop out the seeds and cut the flesh into 1-inch cubes. Dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and squash and cook 3 minutes, stirring, until the squash begins to take on a little color.
Pour in the broth, add 1 teaspoon salt and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat, cover and simmer 20 minutes until the squash mashes easily.
Blend with an immersion blender until completely smooth, adding a splash of water if too thick.
Stir in the cream and nutmeg, warm for 2 minutes and season with salt and pepper.

title: Smoky Black Bean Soup
steps: Drain and rinse the black beans. Dice the onion, mince the garlic and cut the lime into wedges.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion 6 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika and stir 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the beans, broth and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer 15 minutes.
Mash about a third of the beans against the side of the pot, or use an immersion blender for 3 pulses, to thicken the soup.
Simmer 5 more minutes, squeeze in the lime juice and season with pepper.

title: Potato Corn Chowder
steps: Dice the bacon, onion and peeled potatoes into 1/2-inch pieces.
Cook the bacon in a pot over medium heat for 6 minutes until crisp. Remove it and leave 1 tablespoon of fat in the pot.
Add the butter and onion and cook 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the flour and thyme and cook 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in 1 cup water and the milk, then add the potatoes, corn and 1 teaspoon salt.
Simmer on medium-low for 15 minutes, stirring often, until the potatoes are tender and the chowder thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Mash a few potatoes against the pot for extra body, season with pepper and top with the bacon.

title: Smashed Cucumber Salad
steps: Lay a cucumber under the flat of a knife and press firmly until it splits, then tear it into bite-size pieces. Repeat with the second cucumber.
Toss the pieces with 1/2 teaspoon salt in a bowl and let them sit 10 minutes to release their water.
Mince the garlic and whisk it with the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar and red pepper flake until the sugar dissolves.
Drain off the liquid from the cucumbers and pat them gently dry.
Pour the dressing over the cucumbers and toss until evenly coated.
Chill for 5 minutes if you like, then serve cold.

title: Tomato Bread Salad
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F. Tear the bread into 1-inch chunks, toss with 1 tablespoon olive oil and a pinch of salt and spread on a baking sheet.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes, shaking the pan once, until the bread is golden and crisp outside.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges, slice the red onion thinly and tear the basil. Mince the garlic.
Whisk the remaining olive oil, balsamic vinegar, garlic, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the tomatoes and onion and let them sit in the dressing for 5 minutes so they release their juices.
Fold in the warm bread and basil and let rest 5 minutes before serving so the bread soaks up the dressing.

title: Kale Apple Salad
steps: Remove the tough stems from the kale and slice the leaves into thin ribbons. Juice the lemon and core and thinly slice the apple.
Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking often, until fragrant, then roughly chop.
Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, mustard, 1/2 teaspoon salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the kale and massage with your hands for 1 to 2 minutes until it darkens and softens.
Add the apple, walnuts and shaved parmesan and toss gently.
Let it sit 5 minutes to mellow, then serve.

title: Crispy Roasted Chickpeas
steps: Heat the oven to 425 F. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.
Spread the chickpeas on a clean towel and rub them dry, discarding any loose skins. The drier they are, the crispier they will bake.
Toss the chickpeas with the olive oil and salt on a rimmed baking sheet.
Roast 20 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until they look golden and sound dry when shaken.
Mix the smoked paprika, garlic powder and cayenne in a bowl.
Roast 5 more minutes, then toss the hot chickpeas in the spice mix. Cool 5 minutes so they crisp up.

title: Chunky Guacamole
steps: Finely dice the red onion and jalapeño, removing the seeds for less heat. Chop the cilantro and dice the tomato.
Halve and pit the avocados, then scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Squeeze in the lime juice and add the salt, then mash with a fork until mostly smooth but still chunky.
Fold in the onion, jalapeño, cilantro and tomato.
Taste and add salt or lime as needed, since avocados vary in richness.
Serve right away with tortilla chips, or press plastic wrap directly onto the surface to prevent browning.
